title: What is `this`?
prompt: In `Point(int x, int y) { this.x = x; }`, why is `this.` required?
options: The parameter `x` shadows the field `x`; `this.x` names the field explicitly
explanation: When a parameter and a field share a name, the bare name means the parameter. `this` is the current object, so `this.x` is its field. If names don't clash, `this.` is optional.

title: Walk a linked list
prompt: Complete the standard list-walking loop that counts nodes.
explanation: `curr = curr.next` steps to the following node; `null` marks the end. This exact loop opens nearly every linked-list problem.

title: Build a reversed copy
prompt:
Return a **new** linked list holding the values of `head` in reverse order (leave the original list alone). For `1 -> 2 -> 3` return `3 -> 2 -> 1`. An empty list (`null`) returns `null`.

Walk the input with the counting loop, and build the output with the 2-arg constructor `new ListNode(val, next)`.

solution.explanation: Reading the input front to back and *prepending* each value to `result` naturally reverses the order: the last value read ends up at the front. `result` starts as `null`, which becomes the tail's `next`. O(n) time, O(n) new nodes.

hints: Prepending to a list puts things in reverse order. What if you prepend every value you read?
Start with `ListNode result = null;` and walk `curr` from `head` until it's `null`.

title: static semantics
prompt: `static int created` in class `Counter` — after `new Counter(); new Counter(); new Counter();`, what is `Counter.created`?
options: `3` — one shared counter incremented by each constructor
`1` — each object has its own copy
explanation: `static` means one copy shared across all instances — that's why it can count how many objects were made.

title: static nested class
prompt: You declare `static class Pair { int r, c; ... }` inside `class Solution`. What does `static` buy you over a plain `class Pair`?
options: A `static` nested class has no hidden link to a `Solution` object, so it can be created anywhere, even from static methods
Only one `Pair` object can ever exist
The fields `r` and `c` become shared by all Pairs
It makes `Pair` accessible outside the file
explanation: `static` on a nested class doesn't make its fields static. It just detaches the class from the enclosing instance. A non-static inner class carries a reference to its `Solution` and can't be constructed from a static context. Default to `static class` for helpers.

title: Build a class: RunningMax
prompt:
Implement a `RunningMax` class:

- `RunningMax()` — starts empty
- `void add(int x)` — record a value
- `int max()` — return the largest value recorded so far (always called after at least one add)

You need one field to remember the max seen so far. Initialize it to `Integer.MIN_VALUE`.

solution.explanation: State lives in a field; methods read and update it. Starting at `Integer.MIN_VALUE` means the first `add` always wins, even for negative values. Every call is O(1). This is exactly the shape of MinStack and other design problems.

hints: The object has to remember something between calls. What single piece of data is enough?
One `int` field holding the best so far; update it in `add` with `Math.max`.
Initialize it to `Integer.MIN_VALUE` in the constructor so negative inputs work.
